en: The hill is moving in waves. The cattle have decided not to notice.
The moon keeps popping out to check on the forecourt. Still nothing happening.
The sky's putting on a show. The fish, as usual, are not.
The moon switched the mountains on. The heat, however, stays off.
The washing should have come in hours ago. The breeze voted to leave it.
The moon drops in between clouds. It can smell the meat from up there.
The Friendly City never asked to be the Windy City, and yet.
Not one shadow on the field all day. The umpire never had to squint.
Shoes on the blanket corners. The breeze is welcome, the sand isn't.
Walk now or don't walk at all. The Lowveld gives you until seven.
Forgot to switch the electric blanket on in advance. Every. Single. Night.
Those clouds are only passing through. Even the mealies know not to get excited.
A few clouds came along to watch. Also not running.
The evening is tiptoeing in on socks.
The clouds are passing the moon around. The balcony is happy to wait.
Midlands mist: the countryside's privacy setting.
The windpump is doing the morning's work. The grass is just waving it on.
The jacaranda petals are taking the bus too. The breeze bought their tickets.
The sky went from light grey to dark grey. That was the whole show.
Half moon, half cloud, full bin. Tuesday night, as advertised.
Cape Town sends solidarity. And a spare cap.
The foghorn is Sea Point's free white-noise machine.
The whole veld with the colour turned down. The sheep count the same either way.
The clouds stayed late just for the colour. Monday owed everyone that much.
The mountain's tablecloth is only half on. It's Monday, nobody's fully dressed.
The flags are still chatting. The boats have called it a week.
Sun, then cloud, then sun. Even the monkeys can't plan around that.
Sea and sky in matching grey. Only the pier lights made an effort.
The sun is doing admin out here. Heat was not part of the package.
The sun is buffering. Do not refresh the page.
Prettiest blue sky in the country, and it feels like a fridge with a view.
No colours in the sky tonight, just shades of calm.
The windpump doesn't believe in knock-off time. Neither does the dog.
We don't talk about today. Today is over. We're proud of us.
The sun took its time this morning. Worth the wait.
Relax, the mountains are just buffering.
Flags out straight, wine held tight. The deck's version of a calm Monday.
Clouds for the sunset, sprinklers for the vines. The farm arranges its own rain.
Cloud shadows crossing the outfield at a steady walk. Nobody's appealing.
That one little light is someone doing winter correctly: hut, fire, done.
The sprinkler is supposedly for the lawn. Look who's all standing in the water.
The whole city had the same plan tonight. Look at us all.
Break time, and the breeze is doing everyone's hair. Teachers included.
Half the stars are behind cloud. The fairy lights are covering for them.

Cape Town after a front: clean, bright, and honestly freezing.
Every light on the string is swaying. Saturday night has rhythm, barely.
The clouds turned pink right on packing-up time. Nobody packed up.
The shed bulb is tonight's sunset. The cattle accept the downgrade.
The flag's giving the forecast before the surfers do. It says: go.
Clouds today, vibes optional.
Properly cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
Sundowners aren't a luxury in the Lowveld. They're medical.
The tablecloth is pressed and ready for tomorrow's service.
The cattle are home before the colour goes. Sunday ends exactly on schedule.
